Team — quick legal read and suggested compromise language. High-level guidance below; see redline snippets at the end.

1) Assignment vs license: assignment of model or model outputs is high-risk for Redwood — it would constrain our ability to productize models trained on platform signal. Recommended compromise: grant Brightline a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Outputs (defined as model-generated content resulting solely from Brightline’s Inputs) for any internal business purpose, including modification and distribution. This preserves model IP while giving Brightline broad commercial rights in outputs.

2) Training opt-out: Agree to a per-customer training opt-out that prevents Brightline Inputs from being used to train, fine-tune, or evaluate our models. We need an implementation description in the MSA/Order Form (e.g., "Redwood will not use Customer Inputs for training unless Customer expressly opts in via Order Form"). This should be scoped to data identified as Brightline’s Inputs in the Order Form.

3) Evidence checklist: We can provide a defined evidence package pre-go-live: SOC2 Type II report (redacted as appropriate), sample retention/config screenshots for the customer account, and anonymized log samples that demonstrate retention and access controls. For items requiring source-of-truth logs we should limit exposure and use secure link delivery.

4) Executive exception: If Brightline insists on assignment, legal needs an exec-level exception (GC + CEO sign-off). Prepare for that ask; procurement often uses assignment language as leverage.

Redline snippets (suggested):
- New clause (Order Form): "Customer Outputs. Subject to Customer’s compliance with the Agreement, Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to exploit Outputs arising solely from Customer Inputs. "
- Training opt-out (MSA / Order Form): "Customer may elect to opt out of Redwood’s use of Customer Inputs for training models. If Customer elects the opt-out, Redwood will not use such Inputs for training, tuning, benchmarking, or model evaluation without Customer’s prior written consent."
- Evidence clause (Order Form/Procurement SOW): "Prior to go-live Redwood will provide the evidence package described in Exhibit X (SOC2 Type II, retention config screenshots, log samples). Delivery shall be via secure link; Redwood may redact PII and Sensitive Information as necessary.)"

Product follow-up: Karthik, please confirm feasibility and an ETA for opt-out enforcement and the three evidence artifacts above. If we can provide a screen + sample logs, that should satisfy procurement.

—Laura

Emma — thanks for the call earlier today. Per our discussion, Redwood’s recommended compromise (attached as redline_summary.pdf) is below. We think it preserves Brightline’s commercial control over Outputs while protecting Redwood’s ability to operate and productize the platform.

1) Outputs: Redwood cannot assign model IP or transfer rights in the Redwood models. Instead we will grant Brightline a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Outputs that are generated solely from Brightline’s Inputs. This includes internal use and redistribution of Outputs.

2) Training opt-out: We will add a clear Order Form option to opt out of Redwood using Brightline Inputs for model training. If selected, Brightline Inputs will be excluded from any training, tuning, or model benchmarking activities.

3) Evidence package: Prior to PO execution Redwood will provide the following via secure link: (a) SOC2 Type II report (redacted as needed), (b) account retention/config screenshots, (c) two anonymized log samples showing request/response retention and access controls. See attached evidence_checklist.csv for the list and delivery plan.

4) Escalation path: If Brightline requires assignment as written, we will need an executive exception (GC + CEO) and will require a commercial concession (e.g., committed volume or revenue threshold).

Next steps:
- We attached a one-pass redline (redline_summary.pdf) with the language Laura suggested and the evidence checklist (evidence_checklist.csv).
- Please confirm acceptance of the license + opt-out approach by EOD Thu 9/16 so we can prepare final Order Form + DocuSign.
- If you need assignment language, let us know immediately so we can route for exec review (this will add time).
